purpose: Test whether the conventional baseline failure is caused by assuming perfect territorial persistence in the conditional mean, after V2 showed that covariance repair alone cannot achieve party-level calibration without losing sharpness.

revision_trigger.diagnosis: The persistence mean is now the binding assumption. A very wide full-support uncertainty distribution still misses repeated party dimensions, so further global widening is forbidden.

mean_family.name: HIERARCHICAL_TERRITORIAL_PERSISTENCE
mean_family.definition: Within each training transition, decompose each party CLR value into a territory-equal national mean plus a territorial deviation. Fit a no-intercept slope mapping prior territorial deviation to next-election territorial deviation. Fit both party-specific slopes and one pooled slope; shrink party slopes toward the pooled slope using only the training transition. Apply the trained slopes to the held-out transition while keeping the national mean at persistence.

crossfit.fold_A: fit mean slopes and residual uncertainty on 2016->2021; evaluate 2011->2016
crossfit.fold_B: fit mean slopes and residual uncertainty on 2011->2016; evaluate 2016->2021

gates.coverage_gate: All 9 party buckets clear both floors in both folds.
gates.selection: Among coverage-eligible candidates, minimize calibration error, then energy score, then 95% width.
